hero.titolo: Report what's happening in your neighborhood.
hero.sottotitolo: Crime collects public safety reports on a shared map. Each report expires on its own once it's no longer useful.

fase1.titolo: Open the map and pick a spot
fase1.descrizione: Mark where the event happened and choose the most fitting category.

fase2.titolo: The report stays visible until it expires
fase2.descrizione: Each category has a validity period: once it's over, the report disappears on its own.

fase3.descrizione: Suspicious reports can be flagged and are reviewed by the platform's moderators.

footer.tagline: Crime — public safety reports maintained by the community.

faq.sottotitolo: How Crime works, how to use it and what you can report. Tap a question to read the answer.
faq.nessunRisultato: No question matches your search. Try another word.

1.descrizione: Nuisance and quiet: noise, litter, broken lights, illegal parking.

2.descrizione: Against property and suspicious situations: thefts, vandalism, drug dealing, scams.

3.descrizione: Against people: violence, threats, robberies, fires.

faq.chiusura: Didn’t find your answer? Open the map and try it: every screen is meant to be clear, and a wrong report can always be removed from your profile.

aCosaServe.r: Crime is a shared map of public-safety reports. People who live in or pass through an area can report what they see (a theft, loud noise, a broken street light) and others can see what is happening around them. Every report expires on its own when it is no longer useful.

emergenze.d: Can I use it in an emergency?
emergenze.r: No. Crime does not replace emergency services and nobody monitors reports in real time. If you are in danger or something is happening right now, call 112 immediately. On the map you will find the “Emergency” button, which asks for confirmation before starting the call.

simboli.d: What do markers, colours and shapes mean?
simboli.r: Each report is a marker with its category icon. The colour shows severity: scarlet red is high, orange is medium, slate grey (and slightly smaller) is low. A high-severity report created less than an hour ago pulses with a red ring. Tap a marker to open its details; the buttons at the top show a single severity.

alone.d: Why is there a halo around a marker?
alone.r: The event was reported at that spot, but it may have moved nearby since: the soft halo, about 100 metres wide, means the position is approximate. It appears when the map is zoomed in enough.

listaRaggio.r: The “List” button at the bottom shows active reports around you, from nearest to farthest. You can choose the radius (500 m, 1, 2, 5 or 10 km) and filter by severity and category.

posizione.d: Why does it ask for my location?
posizione.r: The blue dot on the map is your location, and the list starts from there. Your browser asks for permission the first time: if you refuse you can still use the map, which starts from a default area. The button at the bottom right takes you back to your location.

tema.d: Can I change theme and language?
tema.r: Yes. From the settings (the gear at the top) you choose the light or dark theme and the language. From your profile you can choose the map theme on its own: same as the app, always light or always dark.

come.d: How do I make a report?
come.r: Tap “Report” at the bottom and move the pin to the exact spot of the event, then confirm. Choose the category (you can search it by name), write a clear description of what you saw and publish. The pin starts at your location, but you can drag it wherever you need.

account.r: You need nothing to look at the map and the list. To publish a report or answer “Is it still happening?” you need a free account: if you are not signed in we take you to the login page and then back to the map.

anonima.r: Yes: by ticking “Publish anonymously” your name is not shown to other users. On non-anonymous reports, registered users see your name and the initial of your surname (for example “Mario R.”); your email is never shown. The report stays linked to your account and the people running the service can see it, so they can moderate.

rimuovere.d: Can I edit or remove a report?
rimuovere.r: Your reports are in your profile, in the “Active” and “Concluded” tabs. From there you can open them on the map or remove them. A published report cannot be edited: if you made a mistake, remove it and create a new one.

scadenza.d: How long does a report stay visible?
scadenza.r: Each category has a validity period, from 4 hours to 3 days: ongoing events last a short time, nuisance problems longer (the list below shows it for every category). After that the report becomes “concluded” and disappears from the map; it stays in the profile of the person who made it.

voto.d: What happens if I answer Yes or No to “Is it still happening?”
voto.r: A Yes extends the expiry (once per category duration, not repeatedly) and resets earlier No answers. When three different users answer No, the report closes. If you are the author, your No closes it immediately: we ask for confirmation because it cannot be undone, and only an administrator can reopen it.

cambiareVoto.r: Yes, whenever you like. In the details you see what you already answered (“You answered: Yes”) and the button you chose is highlighted. After you answer the panel closes and a short message confirms what happened.

quali.r: These are the categories available right now, grouped by severity. The list is the real one from the application: if we add or remove some, it updates here. Next to each one you can see how long a report stays visible.

registrazione.r: From the login page choose “Sign up” and enter your first name, last name, email and a password. Once signed in, opening the home page takes you straight to the map.

profilo.r: In your profile (the person icon at the top) you can see and edit your first and last name, change your password, manage your reports and choose the map theme. You can also sign out from there.

fiducia.d: What are “verified identity” and trust score?
fiducia.r: In your profile you can see whether your identity has been verified. The trust score is an internal value of the service: today it does not limit what you can do in the app.

dati.r: For a report they see category, description, position and time and, only if they are registered and the report is not anonymous, the author’s short name. We never show emails or passwords. Your location is used to show you what is around you.

moderazione.r: Reports are moderated by the people running the service, who can suspend, remove or reactivate a report and keep track of who did what. False or off-topic reports can be removed and accounts that abuse the service disabled.
